description.short_caption: Erythematous swelling over the right sternoclavicular joint.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a close-up view of the right sternoclavicular joint. There is a prominent erythematous swelling with a smooth surface, suggesting localized inflammation. The surrounding skin appears intact without visible ulceration or drainage. The swelling is well-circumscribed and appears tender, consistent with an inflammatory or infectious process.

description.short_caption: Radiograph of the left hand showing bony structures and soft tissue.
description.detailed_description: This is a plain radiograph of the left hand in a posteroanterior (PA) view. The bony structures, including the phalanges, metacarpals, and carpal bones, are clearly visible. The soft tissue outlines are also discernible. No obvious fractures, dislocations, or lytic lesions are apparent in this image. A radiopaque marker labeled 'L' confirms the laterality as the left hand.
visible_findings: clear visualization of phalanges, metacarpals, and carpal bones

description.short_caption: Clinical photograph of the right wrist showing a swollen, erythematous lesion.
description.detailed_description: This image shows the dorsal aspect of the right wrist with a prominent, well-demarcated swelling. The lesion appears erythematous and raised, with smooth overlying skin. There is no visible ulceration or drainage. The surrounding skin shows mild discoloration, but no overt signs of additional lesions or trauma.

description.short_caption: Radiograph of the right hand showing bony abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This is an X-ray image of the right hand. The bones of the hand, including the phalanges, metacarpals, and carpals, are visible. There are signs of bony abnormalities, including possible joint deformities and irregularities in bone structure. A marker indicating 'R' confirms the laterality as the right hand.
